title: Rapid palpitations, muscle cramps and tinnitus
task_type: Rapid palpitations, muscle cramps and tinnitus
summary: A man in his mid-sixties, without known medical comorbidities, presents after 24 hours of recurrent palpitations, breathlessness and ringing in his ears. He denies chest pain, presyncope and syncope. He has increased endurance training over three weeks while preparing for a half-marathon and has developed nocturnal muscle cramps associated with exercise. Blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg. The initial ECG is described in the source interpretation as a regular, wide-complex tachycardia of approximately 250 beats/min. No medication/supplement history, echocardiogram, electrolyte results or response to intervention is supplied.
purpose: Write 180–240 words for a clinician. State the immediate assessment priorities, compare clinically important rhythm explanations and identify the exposure history that could change interpretation or action. Explain how the blood pressure affects the sequence of stabilisation and diagnostic clarification. Do not invent a medication, supplement or later ECG result, name a hidden rhythm as established, or provide drug doses. Give brief justifications for the proposed actions.

case.hidden:
Adaptation, hidden results and review

The initial ECG's rate and regular/wide-complex description are transcribed from the published Interpretation. This supplies a textual reading rather than testing independent ECG interpretation. The diagnostic alternatives, post-intervention panel, subsequently elicited quinine exposure and later course are hidden. The report describes initial synchronised cardioversion, recurrent tachycardia after haemodynamic stabilisation and subsequent adenosine exposing atrial flutter. Focused history later identifies quinine-containing capsules used for cramps. The report's proposed drug mechanism is not presented as known at initial assessment.
case.reference: Prioritise haemodynamic assessment, avoid delaying necessary stabilisation to obtain a diagnostic label, maintain a defensible wide-complex differential and consider prescribed/over-the-counter/supplement exposure in light of cramps and tinnitus.

requirements.presentation_based_rationale: Borderline blood pressure affects action timing; tinnitus and cramp treatment make an exposure review relevant without requiring the name of a hidden product.
